running_head.i: curial. Consil. & Respons. lib. 1. Epist. II.

main_text.p: Sed quia in corporeo carcere clausus, absq; eius adminiculis, aut nihil, aut exigua admodum poteft; omni arte & cura elaborandum eft, ut[?] fui carceris insalubritate, perinde ac illi, qui in peftilenti habitat regione, impeditus, aut etiam tabo aliquo contaminatus, inualidus ac pene inutilis euadat.
Quocirca omnes omnium litterarum amantes, omnium Musarum nomine etiam atq; etiam hortor & oro, ut quàm diligentissime meliori valetudini comparandæ, atq; conseruandæ incumbant.

Etenim mihi videtur Natura de illis iure conqueri posse, qui cùm ab ea temperatissimum corpus adepti sunt; illi præclarum adeo ac utile donum, non contemnunt modò (cuius etiâ D. Apost. Paulus geri vult curam) uerùm etiâ corrumpunt, defœdantq;. 1.Thes-sal.4.4.1.Timoth.5.23. Rom.13. D. Sut.Phys.præf.
Vt Galenum noftrum fcribentem, quantumuis optimas corporis temperaturas otio, alijsq; vitæ & victus erroribus, mirificè deprauari, verum prodidisse conteftentur. In lib. Quod mores animi, &c.
Huic igitur MEDICINA incumbit: tantò honoratior & præftantior, quanto magis Corporis Animiq; robur ac sanitas, aut per se expeti debent, aut voluptatis & felicitatis gratiâ exoptari.
Etenim Ars illa est (Ποιητικὴ Factiua) ufu seu Experientia & Ratione constituta ac inuenta, corporis humani bonam valetudinem custodiendi, perditamq; recuperan-

page.notes: Long s was read as plain s throughout (e.g. "claufus" = clausus, "Confil" = Consil). The word after "claufus" is printed "clausus" with an f-shaped long s; the reading is uncertain. The mark before "fui" is a blotted ligature, read as ut[?]. "IIX." is printed as such and left as printed (for VIII). Greek in XI is a clumsy print and only approximated in Greek letters; treat the Greek word as uncertain. The reference line after IX and the line after "defœdantq;" are placed as they appear, below the text, in italic.
